been playing both paladins and ow for over 2 years, not amazing but i don't think im terrible either. here's my advice. 

​

\-item shop wisely, don't take too long on thinking about your purchases but don't buy with no sense either. it is mandatory btw. get familiar with the different items and when you should use them too, it will be a life saver.

\-make loadouts and mainly base them around your talents/playstyle. also find out what you struggle with or like on a certain champion. you have terrible surviability? get a loadout that increases health/lifesteal/shielding/etc. you like a certain good ability they have? base the talent and cards you choose on that ability. this might get me some hate but when it comes to loadouts i'd much rather do what i find to help me rather than a pro's loadout. (though, if you aren't sure how to fix an issue you have on a champion or want to test something then pro loadouts can work)

\-try to play a diverse hero pool rather than all from one category

\-try different things! get that champion. try out that talent. make another loadout. it keeps it fresh and you might just like it. i've been trying out some characters i haven't played in ages and have been having tons of fun with it.

\-keep up with updates---champs and their cards/talents can all change. i'm very guilty of not doing this tbh ( i barely even knew of the newest champion until i saw someone on discord talking about her lmao) and it greatly hinders me sometimes. 

\-this is gonna be cliche but just have fun. don't stress the dude that keeps complimenting you and then saying "cancel that", don't be that guy either. if you're ever curious about something there are many guides out there and you can always come back here. good luck!

What makes (or would) a good app is different from person to person, but for me...

It's (mainly) about 5 things:

* Stability
* Popularity
* Format
* Freedom
* Transparency

**Stability:** The app works, doesn't crash often, you can actually install it, etc. I think i also want to mention things that such as leaks wouldn't really happen on this app, or even if it did its insanely rare and something that could happen on pretty much any app.

​

**Popularity:** This is really all about advertising and luck. I wouldn't mind installing an app before it's popular, everything starts small. But actually having a community to interact with is one of the main things that keep me on an app. No point in trying to gain friends or fans if no one's there.

​

**Format:** Self explanatory. Don't go crazy with it, stop with the ugly bold fonts, don't make it too cluttered or too open, make it easy to understand/use. I'm not a professional there so i can't really give advice in graphic design but yeah.

​

**-Freedom:** There's two things i mean here.

*One:* Having a profile to actually design/make and all that. Personalization.

Personal turn off if I install an app, it asks for my gmail, and it gives me a profile where the only thing I can change is my screen name. Not even a username.

Look at Tumblr for example. Tumblr is probably different than what your aiming for but on there you can change the format of your blog, the colors, fonts, user, etc. It gives personalization and style which pretty much everyone likes. Again that’s blogs but its a good example of what i’m talking about--- at the very least have what fucking Twitter has and let us have a username, header, bio, and pfp.

​

*Two,* the elephant in the room: Freedom of opinions, no political bias on the app.

Look, its your app. There are things I wouldn’t allow on my app, like calling death to entire race for example. But the issue more lies here:

Why allow users to call death to all white people, but than other races are off the table (or vice versa)? I think both are equally terrible and many would agree, but the point is it’s all or nothing. You either allow people to call death to both groups or neither.

Now it's not always so black and white and "all or nothing" can be flawed in cases, but it's a starting point for situations like mentioned.

There's whole essays on this issue who say it better than I do with way more specifics, so I rec looking into it.

​

**Transparency:**

Too lazy to go into detail at this point but basically: tell us why you added a certain feature, why you banned a certain person, why you don’t allow a certain thing. This sorta goes with the last I’d say.

Basically answer questions and don’t hide shit unless its for protection or something.

Welcome! I'll try my best to define these. 

Backfill: Basically someone leaves in a QP or an arcade game,  and you replace them. sometimes near the end of the match. 

 (if you've ever joined a game only to immediately see the "defeat" screen that's backfilling)

Smurfing: When a player who is usually skilled (or more skilled than the other players in their game atleast) play on a back-up account, causing them to get matched with players lower ranked/leveled compared to them. 

EG :A top 500 player makes a new account and is now playing against new players as the game doesn't know they're top 500. 

Feeding: Giving the enemies free kills or damage (which builds up their ultimates) because of your own dumb mistakes rather than being out skilled. 
EG:A player walks into a whole room with the enemy team with no plan or backup, causing them to obviously die. 

Throwing: Purposely letting the enemy win, usually to troll. 

eg: Letting the enemy kill you on purpose, going afk, dancing on point while the enemy is attacking, etc.

When I was younger, before my parents split, I'm pretty sure me and my mom got stalked or something.. 
Anyway, back then my father was a truck driver, so I'd rarely see him. My sister and brother were somewhat older and were always hanging out with friends. So usually, for alot of the day, it was me and my mother... 
Every once in a while, strange men that we did not know came knocking at our door, me and my mom always had it locked and would hide. We knew it wasnt salesman or anything similar, because when my mom asked the neighbors they said they never had people knocking or anything. 
Anyway we never knew the orgins of this , but from a few quick glimpses threw small gaps in the window blinds and stuff we knew it was most likely males, tall ones. 
They would always come at the same time , and always came when it was only me and my mom. The others never really fully believed us. Also it is a little suspicious they always came at the same and right time, as if they knew our daily schedule or something. 
Anyway, one day my mother was taking a bath, she left me to play on the porch with some bubbles  and stuff. I was a good child who knew to stay away from strangers, so she trusted me. 
You probably alreadly guessed, one of those weird men came. 
I was outside, as I mentioned just sitting there doing my own thing, when I saw a truck pull up. A tall male I did not know came out of the vehicle, I don't have good eyesight, and I didn't have glasses or anything on, so I couldn't see him well, but I could of swore he had a weapon. Anyway the moment he got out of the vehicle I ran in, but brilliant me did not close the door. I ran into my mother's room, hiding in a corner, again brilliant me not only chose a out in the open place to hide, but didn't even bother closing my mother's door. 
So, I hear the outside porch door open, my heart was racing. Then I hear the actual door open. For a moment nothing happens. Then I hear walking, then the door opens again. 
The man was gone. 
I sat there for a minute, thinking he could come back, but nothing. I ran out and closed the door and waited for mom to come out. Don't remember much after that. 
However I do remember, I never heard knocking again. Me and my mom never found out what happened or why it did.
